Definition: from G575 and G1381; to disapprove, i.e. (by implication) to repudiate:--disallow, reject.
BiblicalUsage: To disapprove, to reject after testing — the builders' word. The Son of man must be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes in Luke 9:22 and Mark 8:31, and Jesus quotes the psalm against them in Matthew 21:42: the stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner. Peter turns it around in 1 Peter 2:4 — the living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, and precious.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this is the great reversal of the gospel. Men examined Christ and rejected Him; God examined the same stone and chose Him, and set Him as the head of the corner. Every builder's verdict is provisional until God gives His. What men disallow, God may have already chosen.
